Plot a long state sequence as blocks along a serpentine path

Source: R/sequence_snake.R
sequence_snake.Rd

A sequence snake shows one long categorical sequence, such as the actions in a learning session or a person's daily states over months, as a row of colored blocks, one per position. The row is folded into bands joined by U-turns, and the blocks continue through the U-turns, so a sequence of several hundred positions fits in one panel while the order of positions is kept. Runs, recurrences and changes of state can be followed along the path, as in a sequence index plot of a single sequence (Gabadinho et al., 2011).

sequence_snake() accepts the sequence as a vector, a comma-separated string, a list, or a data frame whose first character or factor column holds the states. Blocks can carry position numbers, state names or other labels, and the path can be annotated with ruler ticks, a label for each band and labels at changes of state. With style = "rug" blocks become thin ticks on a light band, which keeps many positions legible.

For many sequences at once use multi_snake(). For phases defined by start and end dates use timeline_snake(), which builds the monthly sequence and its labels from the dates.

Usage

sequence_snake(
  sequence,
  states = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  rows = NULL,
  band_height = 28,
  band_gap = 18,
  plot_width = 500,
  margin = c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 50, left = 80),
  orientation = "horizontal",
  start_from = "left",
  flow = c("natural", "snake"),
  show_labels = TRUE,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  show_numbers = FALSE,
  show_state = FALSE,
  state_size = 0.35,
  show_ticks = FALSE,
  tick_labels = NULL,
  transition_labels = NULL,
  transition_pos = NULL,
  tick_color = "#333333",
  tick_length = 5,
  tick_size = 0.4,
  style = c("block", "rug"),
  band_color = "#3d3d4a",
  rug_opacity = 0.9,
  jitter = 0,
  border_color = NA,
  block_labels = NULL,
  band_labels = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  background = "white",
  shadow = TRUE,
  text_size = 0.5,
  legend_text_size = 0.8
)

Arguments

sequence

The states in order: a character, factor or integer vector; a single comma-separated string such as "A,B,C"; a list; or a data frame, whose first character or factor column is used. Missing values are dropped with a warning.

states

State labels in legend order. NULL (default) takes them in order of first appearance. Every state in sequence must be listed.

colors

State colors: a vector named by state, or an unnamed vector recycled over states. States missing from a named vector are drawn in grey. NULL (default) uses a built-in qualitative palette.

rows

Number of bands. NULL (default) uses one band per 11 positions, rounded up.

band_height

Height of each band in plot units (default 28).

band_gap

Gap between bands in plot units (default 18).

plot_width

Length of each band in plot units (default 500).

margin

Named numeric vector of top, right, bottom and left margins in plot units (default c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 50, left = 80)).

orientation

"horizontal" (default). "vertical" turns the bands into columns but places the blocks across each column rather than along it, so the horizontal layout is recommended.

start_from

Side on which the first band starts: "left" (default) or "right".

flow

"natural" (default): every band reads in the same direction, like lines of text. "snake": bands alternate direction, so the sequence runs on through each U-turn.

show_labels

Label each band with the range of positions it holds (default TRUE).

show_legend

Draw the state legend (default TRUE).

show_numbers

Print each block's position inside it (default FALSE).

show_state

Print the state name inside each block (default FALSE).

state_size

Text size of the state names (default 0.35).

show_ticks

Draw ruler ticks at block boundaries, outside the bands (default FALSE).

tick_labels

Labels for evenly spaced ruler marks on every band, such as month.abb. Setting them turns on show_ticks.

transition_labels

Labels for the points where the state changes, in order; the first length(transition_labels) changes are labelled.

transition_pos

Positions of transition_labels along the sequence, in blocks; fractions such as 6.5 are allowed. NULL (default) places the labels at the changes of state.

tick_color

Color of ticks and of band and transition labels (default "#333333").

tick_length

Length of ticks in plot units (default 5).

tick_size

Text size of tick, band and transition labels (default 0.4).

style

"block" (default) fills each band with blocks; "rug" draws thin ticks on a light band, suited to sequences with many positions.

band_color

Not used at present; rug bands are drawn light grey.

rug_opacity

Opacity of the rug ticks, between 0 and 1 (default 0.9).

jitter

For style = "rug", vertical scatter of the ticks as a fraction of the band height (default 0, none). The scatter is random; call set.seed() first for a reproducible plot.

border_color

Color of block outlines, or NA (default) for none.

block_labels

Labels for the blocks, one per position. They replace the position numbers, and are drawn below the blocks when ruler ticks are shown.

band_labels

One label per band (length rows), printed below the band, for example a year.

title

Plot title, or NULL (default) for none.

background

Background color (default "white").

shadow

Draw drop shadows (default TRUE).

text_size

Text size of block numbers and block labels (default 0.5).

legend_text_size

Size of the legend text (default 0.8).

Value

The plot is drawn on the current device; the function returns NULL invisibly.

References

Gabadinho, A., Ritschard, G., Müller, N. S., & Studer, M. (2011). Analyzing and visualizing state sequences in R with TraMineR. Journal of Statistical Software, 40(4), 1-37. doi:10.18637/jss.v040.i04

See also

timeline_snake() for dated phases; multi_snake() for many sequences; activity_snake() for event times within days.

Examples

# 75 actions in a learning session
set.seed(42)
actions <- sample(c("Read", "Write", "Discuss", "Plan", "Review"), 75,
                  replace = TRUE)
sequence_snake(actions)

sequence_snake(actions, rows = 5, flow = "snake", show_state = TRUE,
               colors = c(Read = "#56B4E9", Write = "#E69F00",
                          Discuss = "#009E73", Plan = "#CC79A7",
                          Review = "#999999"))


# 400 observations of on- and off-task behaviour as a rug
on_task <- sample(c("On task", "Off task"), 400, replace = TRUE,
                  prob = c(0.8, 0.2))
sequence_snake(on_task, style = "rug", rows = 8)
